messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated 5xx and gateway errors observed for /v1/generate across us-west-2 hosted cluster. Error rate spike ~08:03 UTC. Paging on-call.

Sasha: on it — switching to incident channel. anyone oncall for prefix-cache?

Miguel: I am, looking at metrics now. 5xxs correlate with a huge drop in prefix-cache hit rate starting ~08:02, +evictions on kv-store.

Tara: seeing increased 502s at edge too. Some customers complaining about timeouts when sending long prompts.

Ashley: rolling alerts: 5xx rate at 7% over baseline on /v1/generate; p50 latency up 120ms. Can someone check prefix-cache pod restarts?

Miguel: logs -> `prefix-cache` pods show repeated OOMKills and compact loop errors: `compact: encountered corrupted page at offset 0x3f2` then restart. Eviction storm: TTL lifo purge triggered by compactor.

Sasha: possible corruption + eviction cascade. Plan: (1) enable fallback-to-origin for prefix-cache reads (2) scale up cache capacity or reduce eviction aggressiveness (3) avoid rolling restarts that flush cache until fallback is active.

Jeff: tagging runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-prefix-cache.md (see section "eviction storms").

Miguel: executing admin toggle to enable read-through fallback.

Miguel: ```
# enable read-through fallback, route misses to kv-primary
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/config/cache/fallback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"fallback_enabled":true}'
```

ops-bot: config change accepted by admin-api. fallback_enabled=true by miguel at 2026-03-14T08:07:12Z

Tara: confirming edge fallback is live, sending a few synthetic requests. initial results: 5xxs dropping from 7% -> 3.2% in 90s. Some upstream timeouts remain.

Ashley: while fallback reduces errors, it increases origin load. let's throttle large prefix scans. Can we add a short-term circuit breaker for requests with prefix_len > 512?

Sasha: yes — adding traffic rule via api-gw. Miguel, can you prepare a safe rule?

Miguel: ```
# temporarily block/slow-path long prefix requests
kubectl exec -n infra api-gw-0 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -X POST localhost:9000/rules -d '{\"name\":\"limit-long-prefix\",\"match\":{\"prefix_len\":\">512\"},\"action\":\"503\"}'"
```

ops-bot: rule limit-long-prefix created by miguel at 2026-03-14T08:10:04Z

Jeff: customer impact update: ~12 active customers reported degraded responses, ~4 with transient failures (dedicated clusters). Escalating to SEs.

Sasha: on-call handoff in 10m — Miguel you'll own mitigation, I'll stay for postmortem. Any quick mitigation besides fallback?

Miguel: spinning up two additional prefix-cache replicas on dedicated-hostpool to absorb read load, increasing memory limit to reduce OOMs.```

Miguel: `kubectl scale deployment prefix-cache --replicas=5 -n inference` -> scaled. Adjusting mem limit now.

Ashley: also toggled kv compactor into safe-mode to avoid aggressive compaction that may be triggering corruption. Command: `POST /admin/compactor/mode safe`

Tara: quick synthetic after scale + safe-mode + fallback: 5xxs at 1.1% and p95 latency back to baseline. Gateways still showing some 502s from a subset of customer dedicated clusters — likely due to stale local caches there.

Miguel: running diagnostic on a dedicated cluster (dc-42) that reported 502: found prefix-cache replica with disk I/O errors and repeated corruption messages. Taking that node out of rotation.

Sasha: decision: mark incident sev2 (customer impact, partial degradation), continue live mitigation, notify CX and SEs with current status and ETA for fix.

Jeff: posting brief to customer-status: "We are experiencing degraded responses for some model inference requests due to caching infrastructure instability. Active mitigation in progress and we expect progressive recovery over the next hour."

Miguel: starting cache rehydrate job for affected prefixes: `POST /admin/cache/rehydrate` with prefix list from error logs. This will refill from kv-primary.

Sasha: rehydrate and fallback are reducing errors; need to confirm root cause. logs show compactor hit corrupted pages, maybe caused by race in TTL enforcement + compaction.

Ashley: I have a tentative patch that changes compactor to verify page checksums before deletion and to backoff TTL fast-path. Branch: `fix/compactor-checksum-backoff` -> PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/infra/merge/9876

Tara: good. timeline to deploy patch to prod? we should hotfix after stabilization.

Miguel: current next steps: maintain fallback, keep compactor in safe-mode, rehydrate caches, drain bad nodes, increase pod memory, and prepare hotfix. I'll run postmortem template.

Sasha: handing off to miguel for overnight oncall. I'll stay on watch for the hotfix merge and customer comms. Handing over at 08:20 UTC.

Miguel: taking over. summary for next oncall: cause suspected compactor + TTL race leading to page corruption -> eviction storm -> prefix-cache misses -> elevated 5xxs. Mitigations in place: fallback enabled, compactor safe-mode, scaled replicas, rehydrate in progress, circuit breaker for long-prefix traffic. Owner: miguel.

ops-bot: oncall-handoff: sasha -> miguel at 2026-03-14T08:20:00Z

Jeff: will follow up with SEs and ops to check affected dedicated clusters and collect customer list.

Tara: monitoring: dashboards show sustained improvement, will keep telemetry for 2 hours.

Miguel: patch merged to staging, running integration tests. Plan to deploy to prod after 1h of stable metrics.

Sasha: thanks all. please add any followups to the incident board and tag postmortem owner when we close.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation successful, error rate dropped to normal range. Continue monitoring.

Miguel: marking incident as mitigated, moving to postmortem collection.

Sasha: closing active pager. good job everyone. :tada:
